text:
Sam: quick follow-up to the gateway retry RFC — thinking about adding a lightweight 'x-ci-intent' header that indicates "intent:stream" vs "intent:one-shot" so downstream proxies can choose between connection-hold vs immediate hedging. drawing a quick sketch of tradeoffs.
Claire: do you mean intent as an advisory only, or something that affects admission control & queueing decisions?
Sam: advisory by default. optional policy where tenant can opt-in to strict-mode (gateway enforces: stream intents get pinned to long-lived conns and small prefetched kv slots). want to avoid changing existing contract unless tenant opts in.
Zach: sounds reasonable. curious about how this interacts with trailers & prefetch: if we get a small trailer from upstream saying "prefetch=allowed", do we mutate the intent midstream?
Sam: good q — proposal: treat trailer prefetch hints as "soft signals". gateway may upgrade intent from one-shot->stream if trailer shows longer sequence expected, but never downgrade midstream (to avoid surprising the runtime).
Diego: how do we prevent abuse? a client could spam one-shot requests and then flip to stream to hog connections.
Claire: policy layer: require a short warmup handshake for any midstream upgrade (e.g., token that proves the upstream supports streaming semantics). also limit number of midstream upgrades per tenant per minute.
Zach: implementation note: runtime will need a 3-state conn label: ephemeral / pinned / pinned-upgraded. ephemeral = default short TTL; pinned = reserved pool slot; pinned-upgraded = pinned and marked from midstream upgrade. we'll need metrics for count & durations.
Sam: infra checklist:
- annotate ingress logs: intent header, final intent state, any trailer hints
- etm counters: midstream-upgrade attempts, successful upgrades, upgrade rejections
- add admission policy: maxPinnedPerTenant (configurable per tier)
- backpressure path: when pinned pool exhausted, fall back to soft-hedge with slower rate limit
Diego: small proto example for header passing:
```
GET /v1/chat/stream
Host: api.redwood.ai
x-ci-intent: stream;version=1
```
and trailer hint example:
```
Grpc-Trailer: prefetch=1;prefetch-window=64
```
Claire: one more thought on retries: when a midstream upgrade happens and then the upstream dies, we should prefer model-variant fallback (stateless) rather than retrying the pinned connection path. otherwise we risk long reconvergence times.
Sam: agreed. fallback policy: pinned conn failures -> try compatible lower-memory model on same path -> if not available, fallback to hedged replicated one-shot paths.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/intent-header gating flag enabled in staging. 3788880002 by @Sam
Zach: ack. I'll add the conn-label enum to the runtime PR and wire the metrics. minimal unit tests: simulate midstream upgrade and kill upstream, assert fallback path chosen.
Sam: thanks — can we sync tomorrow 10a to decide config defaults? I'll post brief agenda.
Claire: +1. I'll bring notes on abuse mitigation thresholds.
Diego: +1. I'll prepare a short perf microbench for pinned vs ephemeral slots.
